# Navigation of Gym menu (AH-0MV1BKZ0J00946EX)

## Problem statement

The dev-mode Gym Index (`GymIndex`) lays its launch rows out in three columns
(plain scenes | ENEMIES | Dev Utilities), but keyboard focus moves through
every row as a single linear, wrapping list. The arrow keys therefore do not
match the on-screen spatial layout: Right from the bottom of a column jumps to
the next column's first row, and there is no deliberate way to step
left/right between columns. A keyboard-only developer cannot navigate the
index the way they read it.

## Users

Developers/testers who exercise the gym scenes, and keyboard-only or
accessibility users who expect the in-canvas UI to match its visual layout.

**User stories**

- As a keyboard-only developer, I want **Left/Right** to move focus between the
  three columns, so that I can reach the column I want without tabbing through
  every row.
- As a keyboard-only developer, I want **Up/Down** to move focus within the
  current column, so that I can choose a row in that column predictably.
- As a keyboard-only developer, I want the focused row to stay highlighted and
  **Enter/Space** to launch it exactly as before, so that the new navigation
  does not break activation.
- As a maintainer, I want the grid behaviour to be **opt-in** in the shared
  focus manager, so that every other menu keeps its current linear Tab/arrow
  behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Opt-in grid navigation; existing behaviour unchanged.** The shared
  `FocusManager` (or a small shared helper alongside it) gains an opt-in
  column-aware navigation mode. Scenes that do not opt in keep today's linear
  Tab / Shift+Tab / arrow cycling with wrap-around. *Verification:* the
  existing `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` passes unchanged, and a new test
  asserts the default mode is still linear.
- **AC2 — Left/Right move between Gym Index columns.** With grid navigation
  enabled, **Right** moves focus to the adjacent column on the right and
  **Left** to the adjacent column on the left, wrapping from the rightmost
  column to the leftmost and vice versa. Focus never lands on a non-row
  (title, headers or hint). *Verification:* a unit test in
  `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` asserts the focused column changes on
  ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and wraps at both ends.
- **AC3 — Up/Down move within the current column.** **Down** moves focus to
  the next row in the current column and **Up** to the previous row, wrapping
  within the column (top ↔ bottom). Up/Down never change column.
  *Verification:* a unit test asserts vertical movement and per-column
  wrap-around without leaving the column.
- **AC4 — Uneven columns always land on a valid row.** The columns have
  different row counts (plain scenes: many; ENEMIES: 3; Dev Utilities: 1).
  Moving horizontally into a shorter column focuses a valid, highlighted row
  (clamping rule documented below) — never an out-of-range index or a
  non-row. *Verification:* a unit test drives focus to the bottom of the
  longest column, presses Right into the shortest column, and asserts a real
  row is focused and highlighted.
- **AC5 — Activation, pointer and ESC unchanged.** Enter/Space still activate
  the focused row through the same callback as a pointer click (plain scene,
  Fodder Enemies, Boss, Mini-Boss, Dev Utilities), pointer clicks still work
  for every row, ESC still returns to the main menu, and SHUTDOWN still
  detaches the keyboard listener and clears the focus registry.
  *Verification:* the existing GymIndex activation/pointer/ESC/shutdown tests
  remain green, plus a new test activating a row after moving between columns.
- **AC6 — Hint and documentation updated.** `GYM_INDEX_HINT` and every doc that
  enumerates keyboard navigation describe Left/Right column movement and
  Up/Down row movement. *Verification:* inspection of the hint and the updated
  docs sections.
- **AC7 — Tests, docs and full suite.** New/updated tests cover AC1–AC5. All
  related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. The full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is the **Gym Index screen** (`GymIndex`), **not** the internal menus of
  individual gym scenes and **not** the other menu-style scenes.
- Reuse the shared `FocusManager`; do **not** add a second ad-hoc focus/key
  handler inside `GymIndex`.
- The default (non-grid) behaviour must remain the current linear behaviour
  for every other consumer (`MenuScene`, `GameOverScene`, `PauseScene`,
  `HelpScene`, `LeaderboardScene`, `TelemetryConsentScene`, and the Hangar War
  screens).
- Pointer handlers, ESC-to-menu, row ordering and the column layout (X
  positions) must not change.
- No CI/CD pipeline tests (per intake convention). `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
  (managed by the ship skill).
- No new npm dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` renders three columns and registers every row with
  the shared `FocusManager` in reading order (plain scenes → ENEMIES → Dev
  Utilities). `GYM_INDEX_HINT` currently reads
  `tab/arrows move · enter/space select · ESC returns to menu`.
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` maps Tab / Shift+Tab and **every** arrow key
  onto linear `cycleFocus(±1)` with wrap-around; it has no notion of columns or
  axis. It is used by `MenuScene`, `GameOverScene`, `PauseScene`, `HelpScene`,
  `LeaderboardScene`, `TelemetryConsentScene` and the Hangar War screens.
- `GymIndex` exposes test accessors `listedScenes`, `listedEnemyScenes`,
  `listedDevUtilityScenes`, `getFocusedIndex`, `getFocusedLabel` and
  `getFocusControlCount`. Column X positions are exported as
  `GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` already has a keyboard-navigation block that
  asserts the current linear order and wrap; those arrow assertions will need
  updating to the new semantics (Tab/activation/ESC coverage is kept).
- 2-D/grid navigation was explicitly deferred in AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE (linear
  cycling shipped instead); this item is the follow-up that delivers it.

## Desired change

1. Extend the shared `FocusManager` with an **opt-in** column-aware mode (for
   example `attachKeyboard(scene, { navigation: 'grid', columns: [...] })` or an
   `attachGridKeyboard(scene, columns)` helper). Columns are ordered lists of
   controls (or focus indices) in visual order; the default path stays exactly
   as today.
2. In `GymIndex.create()`, register the existing three columns with grid mode,
   using the same `registerRow` activation callbacks.
3. Implement the horizontal/vertical movement rules (including wrap and
   shorter-column clamping) and keep Enter/Space activation unchanged.
4. Update `GYM_INDEX_HINT`, the module doc comment and the README
   keyboard-navigation / Gym Index sections.
5. Update/extend `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` to cover grid mode while keeping linear mode
   covered.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` — add opt-in grid/column navigation while
  preserving the current linear default.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — opt into grid navigation, pass the three columns,
  update the hint and module doc comment.
- `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` — cover grid-mode movement and confirm the
  linear default is untouched.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — cover Left/Right column movement (with wrap),
  Up/Down within-column movement, uneven-column clamping, activation after a
  column move, and the updated hint.
- `README.md` — update the keyboard-only navigation section and the Gym Index
  section (~lines 391 and ~417) to describe column/row arrows.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §8.5 keyboard-operability note if
  it enumerates Gym Index navigation.

## Related work

- AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE — Gym scenes index not navigable by keyboard (delivered
  linear `FocusManager` navigation; explicitly deferred 2-D/grid navigation).
  *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZT64O0056BRY — Reusable in-canvas focus manager (the shared utility
  to extend). *Completed.*
- AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E — Single enemy gym scene with in-panel selector;
  established the current three-column index layout. *Completed.*
- AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL — Dev Utilities gym scene / column. *Completed.*
- AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9 — Keyboard only control (umbrella). *Completed.*

## Risks & assumptions

**Risks**

- **FocusManager regression.** The utility is used by eight scenes; a careless
  change could alter their arrow-key behaviour. Mitigation: opt-in mode only,
  default unchanged, plus the existing FocusManager tests and the full-suite
  gate.
- **Test churn.** The existing GymIndex keyboard tests assert linear arrow
  order; they must be updated to the new arrow semantics while keeping
  Tab/activation/ESC coverage. Mitigation: keep Tab's behaviour explicit and
  test both models.
- **Uneven-column UX.** A naive clamp can make focus jump unexpectedly when
  moving to a shorter column and back. Mitigation: document the rule and test
  it; sticky per-column row memory is a small, contained follow-up if wanted.
- **Scope creep.** Grid navigation for other scenes (Leaderboard grid, hex
  map) or mouse-free gym internals is out of scope; record as linked
  follow-ups rather than expanding this change.

**Assumptions (documented; reversible)**

- Grid mode is **opt-in** and **GymIndex-only** in this change.
- Left/Right **wrap** between columns (rightmost → leftmost and vice versa),
  matching the existing wrap convention.
- Up/Down **wrap within the current column** (top → bottom and bottom → top)
  and never change column.
- On entering a shorter column, focus **clamps to the last valid row** of that
  column (no per-column row memory in this change).
- **Tab keeps its current linear cycling** through all rows in reading order;
  only the arrow keys become grid-aware.
- Activation (Enter/Space), pointer handling and ESC behaviour are unchanged.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Should Left/Right wrap between columns, or clamp at the outer
columns?**

- Answer: OPEN QUESTION — no operator was available during this
  auto-dispatched intake. **Working assumption:** wrap (rightmost → leftmost
  and vice versa), consistent with the existing `FocusManager` wrap
  convention. **Recommended:** wrap — matches the established focus-cycle
  behaviour and keeps every row reachable with one key. Reversible.

**Q2 — Should Up/Down stay within the current column, or move across columns
at the top/bottom edge?**

- Answer: OPEN QUESTION. **Working assumption:** stay within the column and
  wrap top ↔ bottom. **Recommended:** stay within the column — keeps the
  horizontal/vertical axes distinct and matches the visual layout.

**Q3 — How should focus behave when moving into a shorter column (for example
Dev Utilities has a single row)?**

- Answer: OPEN QUESTION. **Working assumption:** clamp to the last valid row
  of the target column; no per-column "remembered row" in this change.
  **Recommended:** clamp — simplest, predictable and reversible; sticky row
  memory can be added later if it proves useful.

**Q4 — Should Tab remain linear cycling through all rows, or also become
grid-aware?**

- Answer: OPEN QUESTION. **Working assumption:** Tab keeps today's linear
  cycling (backward compatible); only the arrow keys are grid-aware.
  **Recommended:** keep Tab linear — preserves existing muscle memory and all
  current tests for every other scene.

**Q5 — Should grid navigation be a shared opt-in `FocusManager` mode, or local
to `GymIndex`?**

- Answer: **Working assumption:** shared opt-in mode in `FocusManager`, default
  unchanged. **Recommended:** shared opt-in — `FocusManager` is already the
  single focus mechanism for eight scenes and the repo convention is that
  shared behaviour lives once; an opt-in flag avoids a divergent copy while
  protecting other scenes. Research: inspected `src/utils/focusManager.ts`
  (linear-only today) and its consumers; no existing grid mode.

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Minimal implementation

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).
2. Add src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (facade) and a minimal src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts with the menu/attract state.
3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.
4. Extend SettingsRecord with musicVolume/musicMuted and route them independently of SFX.

## Goal (vertical slice)

Extend the proven music path with the Phrygian Dominant combat layer — Combat Motifs A and B and the combat progression — that transitions in from the ambient state at a bar boundary, stays locked to the shared beat grid, ducks under key SFX, and is driven by PlayScene and the gym scenes identically (gym-game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Wave start transitions menu/ambient -> combat at a bar boundary, and Combat Motif A ("Incoming Wave") introduces the combat state.
- [ ] Combat music tempo is coherent with the game beatBpm (locked to it, or documented as intentionally independent), and never fights the player-fire grid.

# Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C

**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** medium · **Reported:** 2026-10-30 (operator, dev tooling) · **Discovered-from:** AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX

**Headline:** `npm run record` keeps the whole run's telemetry in the page's in-memory buffer and only writes it after the wait loop exits cleanly, so closing the browser window instead of pressing Ctrl+C throws `Target page, context or browser has been closed` from `page.waitForTimeout`, exits non-zero with a raw Playwright error, and writes **nothing** — a long human session is unrecoverable. Make an interrupted recording recoverable (a crash-safe partial capture) or at minimum fail with one actionable line naming the file that was not written and the correct stop procedure, and state the stop requirement (and the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form) in the tool's usage text and docs.

## Problem statement

`scripts/record-session.mjs` starts Vite with `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true VITE_TELEMETRY_SINK=jsonl`, launches Chromium, and polls `readRunEndedSignal` in a `while (!stop.requested)` loop with `page.waitForTimeout(options.pollMs)`. The run's telemetry lives **only** in the page's in-memory buffer, exposed through the dev-gated `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor (telemetry never uses `localStorage`, AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3). The buffer is drained to disk — `resolveRecordingOutputPath` → `writeFileSync` — **after** the loop. Two consequences:

- **Browser close or page crash mid-recording loses everything.** The `waitForTimeout` (or the next `page.evaluate`) throws a target-closed Playwright error; `main()`'s rejection handler prints the raw message (`page.waitForTimeout: Target page, context or browser has been closed`) and exits 1. No recording is written, no path is named, and nothing tells the operator that the session is gone or how to avoid it next time.
- **The stop procedure is unstated where it is needed.** `--help` lists `[--auto]` and the docs mention Ctrl+C, but neither the usage text nor the failure path says "closing the browser loses the session; press Ctrl+C in the terminal to save". Related: `npm run record --auto` does not reach the script as a flag (npm consumes it) — the working form is `npm run record -- --auto` — and nothing in the tool's own output says so.

This item is the dev-tooling behaviour on a **local** recording. Page-side streaming of telemetry to the dev server (which would bound the loss at one batch by uploading during the run) is a separate, parked item — see the boundary in *Related work*.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running a human session** — "As a developer, when I record a long human session and I close the browser window (or the page crashes) instead of pressing Ctrl+C, I want whatever was captured to be saved, or at least to be told in one line which file was not written and how to record properly next time — I do not want to discover after an hour of play that the recording is gone."
- **Developer reading the tooling** — "As a developer, I want `npm run record --help` and the recording docs to state the stop procedure (Ctrl+C saves; closing the window does not) and the correct `--auto` invocation, so the mistake is avoidable in the first place."
- **Maintainer of the recording tooling** — "As a maintainer, I want the interruption path to be a testable seam (injected page/fs), so the crash path cannot regress into a raw Playwright stack again."

## Existing state (verified in code, `dev` @ 59d40269a)

- `scripts/record-session.mjs`
  - `main()` builds the output path **after** the loop (`resolveRecordingOutputPath(options.output, options)`) — so even the would-be filename does not exist at crash time; the default name is stamped at write time, not at start time.
  - Poll loop: `while (!stop.requested) { decoded = decodeRunEndedDetail(await page.evaluate(readRunEndedSignal)); if (decoded !== null && options.auto) break; if (Date.now() - startedAt >= options.maxDurationMs) break; await page.waitForTimeout(options.pollMs); }`.
  - `createStopController()` handles SIGINT/SIGTERM only — there is no `page.on('close')`, `page.on('crash')` or `browser.on('disconnected')` listener, and no distinction between stop reasons.
  - The buffer is read once, after the loop, through `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (bounded CDP messages).
  - `finally` closes the browser/server; the loop's target-closed error escapes to the top-level handler, which prints `error.message` and `process.exit(1)`.
  - Usage text (`--help`) mentions `[--auto]` but not the Ctrl+C-to-save requirement nor the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form.
- Reusable seams already in `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`: `readDevTelemetryChunk({ offset, chunkChars })` returns `{ total, chunk }` — a bounded, incremental slice reader with buffer-reset detection — and `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` shows the "total changed ⇒ discard the partial read" rule. Both are plain exported functions, so an incremental checkpoint can reuse them without new page-side code.
- Precedent for the failure UX: `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs` (`salvageFailedCapture`, `formatSalvageMessage`) prints **one** actionable line first (what failed, bytes salvaged, the `.partial.webm` path, next action) and exits non-zero; `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` writes to `<stem>.partial.webm` and renames into place only on success. The recording tool has no equivalent.
- Docs to keep true: `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 (flag table; "On Ctrl+C the tool still exports whatever the sink has already flushed … so an interrupted run yields a partial but valid recording" — true only for Ctrl+C, not for a browser close), and `docs/TELEMETRY.md` L117–122 / L566–574 (the recorder reads the buffer through `window.__aiHellTelemetry`).
- Test coverage today: `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` covers argument parsing, path resolution, the balance artifact and the `--help`/argv entry guard; `scripts/recording.test.ts` covers the pure recording library. **Nothing** exercises `main()`'s wait loop, the stop reasons, or the browser-close path — `main()` is not reachable without a real browser, which is why the crash path is untested.
- Not covered by this item: the page already POSTs the run to `POST /api/telemetry/upload` at run end (`PlayScene._finishRun()`), so a run that **ended** before the window was closed is already stored server-side; the loss is confined to a run closed mid-run.

## Desired change

1. **Crash-safe partial capture (recommended).** Resolve the output path **before** the browser launches. While recording, checkpoint the page buffer to a documented partial file next to it (`<output>.partial.jsonl`) on an interval (`--checkpoint-ms`, default 15 000 ms, `0` disables), appending **only new bytes** through the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop, and restarting from offset 0 when the reported `total` shrinks (the game started a new run — never mix two runs in one file, mirroring `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`). On a clean stop (Ctrl+C, run end, `--max-duration`) write the final file exactly as today and remove the partial. On a browser close / page crash, finalise the partial as the salvaged session and print one actionable line naming it.
2. **Actionable failure when nothing was captured.** If no bytes were captured (or the buffer is unreachable), print exactly one actionable first line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was **not** written and the correct stop procedure, and exit non-zero. A raw Playwright target-closed message must never be the only diagnostic.
3. **Usage and docs.** `--help` and the docs state: press Ctrl+C in the terminal to finish and save; closing the browser window ends the recording and (at best) salvages a partial file; `--auto` must be passed after `--` (`npm run record -- --auto`).
4. **A testable seam.** Extract the wait/finalise logic into exported, injectable functions (page `evaluate`, fs writes, clock) so the crash, salvage and clean-stop paths are covered hermetically in `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — no real browser in the suite.

**Recorded design decisions (settle at review if the producer prefers otherwise; none blocks intake):**

- **D1 — Local checkpoint, not page streaming.** The fix stays inside `scripts/` (CLI-side). Streaming telemetry to the dev server mid-run is AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD and is out of scope; if that lands first, this item's checkpoint becomes redundant and the salvage message can point at the server-side partial (a follow-up, not part of this work).
- **D2 — Salvage-then-message, not message-only.** The item's own AC1 allows either branch; the recommendation is to implement both, so a long session is actually recoverable and the message path still covers "nothing captured".
- **D3 — Partial path.** `<resolved output>.partial.jsonl` (e.g. `recordings/session-2026-10-30T21-18-30-585Z.jsonl.partial.jsonl`), inside the already-gitignored `recordings/`. A salvage must never overwrite an existing final recording — use a collision-safe name (numeric suffix) if the target exists, mirroring the dev-upload plugin's collision-safe storage.
- **D4 — No balance artifact for a salvaged partial.** `balance-stats.json` is written only for a clean stop; a salvaged partial is an interrupted run, not a completed one, and the message says so.
- **D5 — Exit codes.** `0` on a clean stop; `1` (non-zero) on an interrupted/crashed recording, whether salvaged or lost — parity with `capture-salvage`.
- **D6 — Default filename stamp becomes the start time.** Resolving the path up front is required for the partial path; the only visible effect is that the default `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` stamp names when recording started.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser close mid-recording never silently discards the session.** When the page/browser closes (or crashes) during the wait loop, the recorder writes whatever telemetry had been captured — at least the last checkpointed records, each a complete newline-terminated record that parses through the existing recording reader (`parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`), never a half-written line — to the documented partial path (`<output>.partial.jsonl`, collision-safe) and prints **one** actionable line naming that path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure; when nothing was captured it prints exactly one actionable line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was not written. No Playwright target-closed message is the only diagnostic, and the process exits non-zero. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to today's output, no partial file remains, and the exit code is unchanged.

All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Scope ladder.** Only `scripts/record-session.mjs`, a new `scripts/record-session.test.ts`, small additions to `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` and the two docs above (+ a `.d.mts` update if a new export needs it). **No** changes under `src/`, no new page-side API, no dev-server/upload-protocol change (AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD), no change to the telemetry schema.

- **Risk — breaking the clean path.** Touching the write path could rename or relocate the default output; AC1 requires byte-identical output on a clean stop, and `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` keeps the path-resolution assertions green.

- **Q — Is the session recoverable some other way (server-side upload, `localStorage`)?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): no for a mid-run close. A run that *ended* before the window was closed is already stored as `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` by the upload plugin.
- **Q — Does a salvage/partial precedent exist in this repo?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): yes, for video capture — `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` writes `<stem>.partial.webm` and renames on success; `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs` emits one actionable first line (failure, bytes, path, next action) and exits non-zero (AH-0MVNT26AQ005LDNS, AH-0MVNT29MC008BQPY). # Checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 1 (interruption seam and hermetic crash-path tests).

## Goal

As a **developer recording a long human session**, when I close the browser window (or the page crashes) instead of pressing Ctrl+C, I want whatever was captured saved to a documented partial file, so an hour of play is not lost outright.

The run lives only in the page's in-memory buffer (`window.__aiHellTelemetry`); today `main()` drains it to disk once, after the wait loop, so a closed page has nothing to read. Checkpoint the buffer incrementally to `<output>.partial.jsonl` while recording and finalise that partial as the salvaged session when the page dies.

## Scope

- Resolve the recording output path (`resolveRecordingOutputPath`) **before** the browser launches, so the partial path exists at crash time; the default `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` stamp becomes the **start** time.
- Add `--checkpoint-ms MS` (default `15000`, `0` disables) to `parseRecordArgs`, the flag table and the `--help` block.
- Checkpoint writer: on each interval, read **only new bytes** via the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop (reuse the seam; never a whole-buffer single CDP message — AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH), append only up to the last newline (never a half-written record; carry the remainder into the next read), and restart from offset 0 when the reported `total` shrinks (the game started a new run — never mix two runs in one file, mirroring `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`).
- On a `target_closed` stop, finalise the partial as the salvaged session: collision-safe name (numeric suffix) so a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (mirror the dev-upload plugin's collision-safe storage), print **one** actionable line naming the partial path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure, exit 1. Do **not** write `balance-stats.json` for a salvaged partial.
- On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`): write the final file exactly as today, remove the partial, write `balance-stats.json` as today, exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser close mid-recording never silently discards the session.** When the page/browser closes (or crashes) during the wait loop, the recorder writes whatever telemetry had been captured — at least the last checkpointed records, each a complete newline-terminated record that parses through the existing recording reader (`parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`), never a half-written line — to the documented partial path (`<output>.partial.jsonl`, collision-safe) and prints **one** actionable line naming that path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure; the process exits non-zero. The checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing), and a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording — both proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to today's output, no partial file remains, the exit code is unchanged, and no `balance-stats.json` is written for a salvaged partial.
2. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves the checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing).
3. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (collision-safe numeric suffix).
4. `--checkpoint-ms` (default 15000, `0` disables) is parsed, covered by `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` argument-parsing assertions, and passed through to the checkpoint writer.
5. The checkpoint appends only new bytes through the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop — no per-tick full re-read of the buffer, no unbounded in-process buffering — and every written line parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl`.
6. A salvaged partial and its message are additive: the clean-path success output, `balance-stats.json` and exit code are exactly as today.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — output path resolved up front, `--checkpoint-ms`, checkpoint writer, salvage finaliser, stop-reason handling.
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — checkpoint append/reset and no-overwrite tests.
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts` — declarations for new exports and the `checkpointMs` option.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (reused, not modified).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — flag row added to the table (prose/behaviour documented in child 3).

## Notes

- Recordings and partials stay under the gitignored `recordings/`; tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs.
- Long-run cost risk: one CDP round-trip plus a small append per interval; the final read still uses the existing whole-buffer chunked reader. Measurement is child 4.

As a player, I want occasional **special missions** whose rewards are special (a new hull type with extra hit points or extra upgrade bays, rather than another currency drop), so that the ring is never a six-chore checklist.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2). Deliberately **out of scope** for Build Candidate D's MVP (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE); captured so the design intent is not lost.

## Scope

- A special-mission hex/mission type with a reward outside the shipped salvage currencies: a new hull type (extra hit points or extra upgrade bays) is the reference example.
- Must reuse the shipped deployment path (`PlayScene` + `src/scenes/core/`) and the pure hangar economy; no second run implementation (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- Known-ahead intel applies: the reward is visible before the player commits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A special mission is offered, described (reward known ahead) and completable through the shipped run.
- The reward is a hangar entry with a real, persistent effect under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload (no new storage key).
- Gym coverage: the reward/economy behaviour is exercised by `GymHangar` (same code as the game).
- Tests pin the reward, the gating and the persistence round-trip; full suite green.

# Goal

As a player, I want **upgraded defending bots** with special skills that are more effective against certain enemy or boss types, so that what I leave in a hex is a choice rather than a number.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2). Deliberately **out of scope** for Build Candidate D's MVP.

## Scope

- Extend the defending-bot model (currently `HexDefender`: hull id + derived `defenceRating`) with special skills that modify the algorithmic defence resolver against certain attacker/boss types.
- The resolver stays **pure and arithmetic** (`src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`): no simulated battle, no live defence (design of record).
- The defence report must keep showing the numbers that produced every hold and fall, including any skill modifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bot skill changes the resolved defence against a matching attacker type and is visible in the defence report's numbers.
- Skills are pure data + pure resolver inputs; determinism (same seed/payload → same record) is preserved and asserted.
- Gym coverage: `GymHexWar` exercises the same resolver code as the game.
- Tests pin the skill effect, the report rendering and determinism; full suite green.

# Goal

As a player, I want later rings to introduce **variety** — per-hex personalities, contracts and ring landmarks — so that ring *n* is not the same six chores at a higher aggression.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2). Deliberately **out of scope** for Build Candidate D's MVP; the MVP's variety comes from known-ahead intel (boss, weaknesses, grant) and the rush/grind playstyle trade.

## Scope

- Per-hex personality: authored data that changes how a hex's boss/deployment behaves (data-driven, no divergent scene code).
- Contracts: an optional, visible objective on a hex with an extra reward.
- Ring landmarks: authored ring content that changes the ring's shape or a hex's meaning.
- All of it must remain authored data (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` / CSV seeds) consumed by the existing pure ring, resolver and deployment modules; adding a ring stays a data change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each variety axis is data-authored and consumed by the shipped pure modules; no second deployment, resolver or map implementation.
- Known-ahead intel publishes the variety before the player commits.
- Ring validation rejects malformed authored variety loudly (as `validateRingDefinitions` does today).
- Gym coverage: `GymHexWar` exercises the same code as the game; tests pin each axis and the full suite is green.

## Problem

`src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` » `records the measured ring timings and their tolerance` pins the four measured ring-timing means as literals:

```
expect(spec).toMatch(/49\.2/);
expect(spec).toMatch(/109\.0/);
expect(spec).toMatch(/34\.1/);
expect(spec).toMatch(/62\.6/);
```

The GDD §8.2 table those assertions guard is a *transcription* of `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (the artifact the same test already asserts is cited). So every legitimate arena recalibration requotes the artifact and the GDD together, and strands the guard until someone hand-edits four more numbers — which is exactly what happened twice:

- AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0 (ring-2 budget/measurements) — no, stale only after the wrap-aware bot landed;
- AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG (wrap-aware bot) raised the measured grind 91.6 → 109.0 min;
- AH-0MW09QIJU000DAGT (commit `a7c57da1`) recalibrated the ring-2 window to 90–120 min and regenerated the artifact, leaving the guard red until commit `032d96e9`.

The failure was caught (good), but the literals are the wrong source of truth: the guard should assert *agreement with the artifact*, not a copy of it.

## Desired change

In `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`:

1. Read `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (the path the guard already requires the GDD to cite) and derive the expected one-decimal mean for each `ringIndex`/`strategy` pair (`1-grind`, `2-grind`, `1-rush`, `2-rush`) from `summary.totalMinutes.mean.toFixed(1)`.
2. Assert the GDD §8.2 prose quotes each of those four values with its unit (`<mean> min`), so the GDD can never drift from the artifact.
3. Keep the window (40–60, 90–120) and tolerance (±2 / ±3 min) assertions explicit — those are design values owned by `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` / `RING_TIMING_TOLERANCE_PERCENT`, not measurements.

A working implementation was written and verified green (full suite 419 files / 9517 tests) during AH-0MW0J01VV0054BRR but dropped because the sibling item landed the literal-pinning form first; the parked commit is `9467a48a` (ref `refs/wip/AH-0MW0J01VV0054BRR`) if the shape is useful.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The guard's four measured-mean assertions are derived from `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`; no measured-mean literal remains in the test.
2. Editing a mean in the artifact alone (without the GDD) fails the guard; editing the GDD to a value the artifact does not hold fails the guard.
3. The window and tolerance assertions are unchanged and still pass.
4. Full project test suite passes.
data.title: Derive the ring-timing docs guard's measured means from the committed baseline artifact

## Problem

`npm run validate-experience -- <report>` writes `experience-out/experience-validation.json` and `experience-out/experience-validation.md` into the working tree. Add `experience-out/` to `.gitignore` so validation output stays a local artefact, and remove the two accidentally committed files from the repo (`git rm --cached` semantics — keep them on disk for anyone relying on them locally). Optionally add a one-line note to `docs/BALANCING.md` / `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` that the output directory is git-ignored.

- [ ] `.gitignore` lists `experience-out/` beside `eval-output/`.

- [ ] `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` (or `docs/BALANCING.md`) states that the output directory is git-ignored.

# Dev write path for `weapon-levels.json` (rhythm Save in the tuning panel)

discovered-from:AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7 — deferred by the option (b) scope decision.

## Goal

Let designers persist rhythm edits from the browser into `src/data/weapon-levels.json` and hear the change without an editor, completing the "no TypeScript, no editor" story for fire cadence.

As a designer, I want to tune a weapon's Euclidean rung (`k`, `n`, `rotation`) with a live preview and press **Save**, so I can iterate on rhythm feel without editing JSON by hand.

## Context

- AH-0MW0Q1TQV009M8AO (child of AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7) moves `WEAPON_EUCLIDEAN_LADDER_SPECS` into `src/data/weapon-levels.json` with a code-default fallback, and the tuning panel (AH-0MW0Q1HMH0037RNC) shows the ladder read-only with a rung preview. Hand-edit only was a deliberate scope cut, not a design preference.
- The write-back precedent already exists: `vite/plugins/botTuningPlugin.ts` (dev-only `GET`/`PUT` JSON middleware with validation, `apply: 'serve'`), mirroring `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` for CSV.

## Deliverables

- Dev-only JSON write API for `src/data/weapon-levels.json` in the `botTuningPlugin` style: `GET` the committed file, `PUT` a weapon's rung list, atomic temp+rename write, `400` with a diagnostic on invalid payloads (non-integer `k`/`n`, `k > n`, `rotation` outside `[0, n)`, decreasing density, unknown weapon id), file byte-identical on rejection.
- Panel controls: per-rung `k`/`n`/`rotation` editors with live preview, **Save** and **Save As** (duplicate rung sets onto another weapon), re-read of the ladder after a successful write so the running scene reflects it.
- Production/static builds remain read-only with a visible message; no fetch is attempted.
- Tests: plugin upsert/reject/atomicity in a temp dir; panel payload building; re-read updates `resolveWeaponPattern` output; read-only mode disabled.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Under `npm run dev`, changing one rung of `cannon` in the panel and pressing Save updates `src/data/weapon-levels.json` and the live rhythm changes without a restart.
2. All invalid payload classes above are rejected with a diagnostic naming the weapon, rung index and field, and the file is unchanged (asserted byte-for-byte).
3. A monotonicity violation (density decreasing across rungs) is rejected rather than silently re-timed.
4. Read-only build disables Save with a visible message and does not throw.
5. `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and the changed-scope tests pass.

## Key files

- `vite/plugins/botTuningPlugin.ts` (pattern reference)
- `vite/plugins/weaponLevelsPlugin.ts` (new) + tests
- `src/core/weaponLevelsStore.ts` (new, client re-read seam) or an extension of the existing config store pattern
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponTuning.ts` (add the editable rhythm surface)
- `src/data/weapon-levels.json`

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` > `--watchdog bounded-runtime guard (AC2/AC6)` > `aborts with exit 124, names the phase and restores the CSV` failed once during a full unit run with:

```
AssertionError: expected [ 'enemy-configs.csv.tune-journal' ] to deeply equal []
 ❯ scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts:130
```

The test asserts that no `*.tune-journal` file remains in `src/data` after the CLI aborts. It reads the **real** `src/data` directory, so the assertion observes any other process/vitest worker that is momentarily holding a journal there. Re-running the same suite immediately afterwards was green (4431 passed), so it is a flake, not a regression.

## Goal

Make the watchdog assertion observe only its own run: point the CLI's CSV/data root at a per-test temp directory (or have the assertion filter to the journal the run under test created), so a concurrent worker's transient journal cannot fail it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The test no longer reads shared mutable state in `src/data` (per-test temp data root, or an owner-scoped journal name).
2. Two concurrent full-suite runs of `npm test` leave the test green.
3. Every other `evaluate-tune-progress` assertion still holds.

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` edits a tracked balance CSV in place and journals the pre-edit bytes beside it (`src/data/<file>.tune-journal`). Both paths are process-global, not per-run:

1. **Startup reconcile steals a live journal.** `main()` reconciles `<csv>.tune-journal` before anything else (crash recovery). A journal is written before the edit and removed after the restore, so it exists for the whole candidate sweep of a *running* process — a second `--tune` run on the same CSV reconciles it, restoring the CSV underneath run 1.
2. **Two runs interleave edits.** Run 2 writes its own journal over run 1's, then restores from run 2's bytes while run 1 continues its candidate sweep against a file run 2 may have rewritten.

Discovered while fixing AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS: the `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` watchdog case asserted "no `*.tune-journal` anywhere in `src/data`", which failed when a sibling suite in the same parallel Vitest run held a journal at the same shared path. The suite was fixed for the shared path (the assertion is now scoped to the run's own pid), but the product-level hazard remains for real concurrent CLI invocations.

## Impact

Two designers (or a designer plus a scripted tuning sweep) tuning the same balance CSV at once can silently produce a comparison against the wrong CSV bytes, and the crash-recovery journal can be consumed by the wrong run. Single-run usage is unaffected.

## Suggested approach

Pick one, cheapest first:

- **Lock file**: an exclusive `<csv>.tune-lock` (O\_EXCL) held for the whole run, with a bounded wait and a clear exit-2 diagnostic naming the holder pid. The journal's pid is already recorded, so the holder is identifiable.
- **Refuse concurrent runs**: on `writeJournal`, if a journal exists whose pid is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), abort with exit 2 naming that pid instead of overwriting it.
- **Per-run temp CSVs**: out of scope — `--tune` deliberately edits the tracked file so the candidate sweep reads it through the shared config store.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent `--tune` runs on the same CSV cannot interleave: the second either waits (bounded) or exits non-zero with a diagnostic naming the holding pid.
2. A live journal is never reconciled by another process: crash recovery only consumes a journal whose pid is dead.
3. `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` still pass, including the pid-scoped journal assertions added by AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS.
4. `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the concurrency rule alongside the crash-safe journal section.
5. Full suite passes (`/skill:test`).

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS (the test-failure item that surfaced the shared-path race).
data.title: Serialise concurrent --tune runs on the same balance CSV (shared journal path)

## Goal

Make the dev-only telemetry recorder cheap enough that it does not distort a measured run.

**User story:** As a developer profiling the game, I want the dev telemetry recorder to stay out of the frame budget, so a profile measures the game and not the recorder.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

CPU profile of \`PlayScene\` level 10 demo (60 s, desktop headless Chromium), with the dev recorder enabled:

- \`sanitiseObject\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:93\`) 0.18 % of the measured window, \`sanitise\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:65\`) 0.15 %, \`utf8ByteLength\` (\`src/telemetry/devUpload.ts:180\`) 0.14 %, \`write\` (\`src/telemetry/sinks.ts:50\`) 0.08 %, \`deepFreeze\` (\`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:459\`) 0.16 % — **~0.7 % of the window / ~7 % of JS**.
- The same run logged a skipped run-end upload: 15.8 MiB of run telemetry exceeded the 8 MiB browser→node message cap, so the recorder was serialising a payload it then discarded.

## Scope

- Avoid serialising/redacting a payload that will be discarded for exceeding the upload cap (check the size first, or stream/bound the recording).
- Keep redaction guarantees intact: no unredacted payload may ever reach a sink.

## Out of scope

- Production telemetry behaviour (the recorder is dev-only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run whose telemetry exceeds the upload cap no longer pays the full serialise+redact cost before discarding (verified by a test on the size-guard seam).
2. Redaction tests still pass (no path skips redaction for a payload that is written).
3. In the same profiled demo run, the telemetry bucket share is measurably lower, with the before/after numbers recorded on this item.
4. Full project test suite passes.
data.title: Dev telemetry serialisation costs ~5 % of JS during demo runs

## Goal

Reduce the attract-mode (demo) bot's per-frame cost at late-game load, so the shipped attract screen does not pay more for its pilot than the game pays for its simulation.

**User story:** As a player watching the attract screen, I want the demo to stay smooth at late-game load, so the menu experience matches the game's.

## Summary

The stress gym's `getPerformanceCounts()` override carries a comment claiming the mineral count is always zero, but the hardware-GPU verification runs (AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P) recorded non-zero live minerals in every report.

**Discovered from:** AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P (hardware-GPU desktop verification runs).

## Evidence

`src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts:291`:

> `minerals` is 0 because this gym deliberately seeds none.

Measured `counts` from the four 60 s hardware-GPU reports (`counts` sampled every 250 ms, 237 samples each):

| Host | Run | minerals peak | minerals mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| desktop browser | 1 | 8 | 1.20 |
| desktop browser | 2 | 7 | 2.11 |
| Electron | 1 | 1 | 0.55 |
| Electron | 2 | 2 | 0.95 |

The gym config does set `minerals: false` (`src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts:207`), so the field starts empty — the non-zero values accumulate during the window (most plausibly salvage dropped by enemies destroyed on contact with the player ship), which the comment does not anticipate.

## Expected behaviour

Either the comment/doc statement is corrected to "the field starts empty (no seeding) and can accumulate a handful of drops", or the gym actively clears the mineral field so the measured load really is enemies + bullets only. The first is documentation-only; the second changes the measured scene, so it needs its own before/after run.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts` no longer claims the mineral count is always 0, or the gym's measured mineral count is 0 in a 3 s guard-check run — one of the two, with the choice recorded.
2. `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`'s statement about the stress gym and minerals is consistent with the behaviour actually implemented (and with the counts blocks already published for AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P).
3. If the gym is changed to clear the field, a `--seconds 60 --warmup 3` `GymPerformance` run is recorded showing the scene still holds 100 enemies and ~200 live bullets.

## Out of scope

- Re-measuring the hardware baselines — they are recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` and are not invalidated by a comment fix.

**Headline:** A performance-testing skill that sweeps enemy counts in 50-enemy steps with semi-random, representative loadouts to determine the playable enemy count ceiling with reproducible FPS data.

## Problem / goal

The repo can measure one fixed load (`GymPerformance`, exactly 100 enemies with
live fire — AH-0MVXV0DT50028RF8) but there is no repeatable way to answer "how
many enemies can we actually hold at a playable frame rate?". The producer has
to pick the load by hand, run the harness several times, and reconcile the
numbers themselves.

As the producer, I want **a performance testing skill** that automatically
walks the enemy load upward in 50-enemy steps until the game stops being
playable, so I get a headroom curve (min / max / average FPS per load) from one
command instead of a series of ad-hoc runs.

## Expected behaviour

Invoking the skill (e.g. `/skill:perf-sweep`, final name to be decided at plan
time) runs a **sweep**:

1. **Load steps of 50 enemies**, starting at 50 (`50, 100, 150, …`).
2. At every step the measured load is **enemies that both shoot and dive** —
   live fire and diving behaviour on screen, not idle targets. The **mix of
   shooting and diving archetypes varies per step**, chosen from a fixed seeded
   roster (the existing stress gym already includes `diver` and `raider`), and
   the mix is recorded with the step.
3. At every step the **player has a semi-random, representative loadout**
   (defined concretely under *Resolved design decisions*): weapons drawn from
   **each broad weapon category**, **at least one power-up**, filled up to the
   shipped six-slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`). Weapon and power-up
   **levels are not maxed**: they are set to a level *representative of the
   campaign level a hex of the configured aggression deploys at*. The chosen
   loadout and its levels are recorded with the step.
4. The **player fires** (auto-fire on) with the full loadout — the measured
   frame cost includes the player's own bullets and kills.
5. Each step is measured for **at least 15 seconds** (warm-up excluded from the
   measurement window, and reported).
6. Per step record **min, max and average FPS** (plus p50/p95 frame time, long
   frames, and live enemy/bullet counts — the harness already produces these).
7. **Iterate until a step's average FPS is below 30**, then stop: that step is
   the reported failure point and the previous step is the last playable load.
   A hard ceiling (e.g. 400 enemies) and a total-run budget guard against a
   runaway sweep.
8. **Report the results to the user** at the end: a summary table of every step
   (enemy count, loadout + levels, shoot/dive mix, min/average/max FPS,
   verdict) plus the headline ("playable to N enemies; first failure at M with
   average X FPS") and the path to the machine-readable JSON report.

## Resolved design decisions (producer answers)

These replace the five open questions from the seed description. Answers are
the producer's, with the concrete, testable interpretation the implementation
must pin.

1. **Skill location — project-local.** The skill lives in the repo at
   `.pi/skills/<skill-name>/` and may reference the repo's harness. Editing
   `.pi/` is normally restricted; this item is the explicit instruction to add
   this skill. *Producer answer: "project-local".*

2. **"Full loadout" — semi-random and representative.** The loadout is built
   through the shipped seams (`Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` per level and
   `Player.collectPowerUp(id, permanent)`), never a test-only fork, and fills
   at most the six-slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`).
   - **Broad categories** to draw from (one weapon from each, subject to the
     six-slot cap): *conventional projectile* (`spread`, `dual`, `rapid`),
     *beam/hitscan* (`wave_laser`), *area-of-effect* (`nova`, `mortar`, `arc`),
     and *exotic/positional* (`ricochet`, `cluster`, `options`, `rear_guard`,
     `broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`). The permanent
     `cannon` is always present as the base weapon.
   - **At least one power-up** from `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`.
   - **Remaining slots** are filled with a seeded random choice of the
     remaining weapons/power-ups, still respecting the six-slot cap.
   - **Levels are not maxed.** Weapon collection level and power-up level are
     derived from the campaign level a hex of the configured `--aggression`
     deploys at (`deploymentLevelForAggression(aggression)` →
     `hexAggressionLevel`, campaign level 1–`MAX_LEVEL` = 1–10): a
     representative upgrade index scaled from the fraction of the campaign
     climbed, clamped **below** each weapon's upgrade cap, so a late aggression
     is strong-but-not-maxed. The exact scaling constant is a plan-time tuning
     constant; the rule and every derived level are recorded per step.
   - *Producer answer: "Semi-Random, include weapons from each broad category and
     at least one power-up. Don't max the levels — make them somewhat
     representative of the level they would be if attacking a hex of the
     defined aggression."*

3. **Shoot-and-dive mix — vary it.** Each step's enemy roster mixes shooting
   and diving archetypes, with the **proportion varying per step** (seeded, and
   recorded), rather than one fixed ratio throughout the sweep. The roster is
   fixed at step setup so the load is constant for that step. *Producer answer:
   "vary them".*

4. **The player shoots — yes.** Auto-fire is enabled with the step's loadout,
   so the measured load includes player bullets and kills. Enemies are **not**
   made invulnerable: the step spawns its target N at step start and the live
   enemy/bullet counts are recorded through the window (N is the peak/target
   load). *Producer answer: "Yes".*

5. **Step comparability — fixed seed + fixed duration.** The sweep runs an
   **as-played, deterministic mode**: one seed for the whole run and a fixed
   per-step duration mean the same seed reproduces the same loadout sequence and
   (with the scene's own seeding) the same evolution. Kill-free/invulnerable
   enemies are explicitly *not* used. The report records the seed, the fixed
   duration and the "as-played" mode. *Producer answer: "fix seed + duration".*

## Design outline (to be confirmed at plan time)

- Reuse the existing harness rather than writing a second one:
  `scripts/measure-performance.mjs` (`perfProbe`, `--seconds`, `--warmup`,
  `--cpu-throttle`, `--scene`, `--out`) and its pure maths in
  `scripts/perf-report.mjs`.
- The scene must accept an **enemy count parameter**, a **semi-random loadout
  setup** and a **per-step shoot/dive mix**. Options to choose between at plan
  time: (a) parameterise `GymPerformance`/`GymFormationScene` (it already takes
  `config.count` and `buildOffsets(count)`) rather than adding a scene; or
  (b) add a sweep gym. Preference is (a) — one scene, one code path, no
  divergence — with the parity matrix updated only if a new scene is genuinely
  required.
- The loadout must be applied through the shipped/shared path (no test-only
  re-implementation of weapon or upgrade behaviour), so the measured frame cost
  is the frame cost a player would pay: `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)` L times
  for a weapon level L, and `Player.collectPowerUp(id, true)` for a power-up
  level, respecting the six-slot cap.
- The sweep orchestration should be a small, unit-testable pure planner (step
  list, stop rule, summary) driven by a thin CLI/script, so the stop rule and
  summary are tested without booting a browser.
- Loadout selection and the shoot/dive mix must be **seeded and recorded**, so
  a run can be reproduced (`seed` in the report; same seed → same loadout
  sequence and same mixes).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A performance-testing skill exists, is discoverable by name, and its
   documentation states the sweep, the load definition, the 15 s minimum
   measurement window and the stop rule.
2. One command runs the whole sweep unattended on the reference host: enemies
   in 50-enemy increments, each step with enemies that shoot **and** dive (mix
   varying per step), the player firing a **semi-random** loadout that draws a
   weapon from each broad category and **at least one power-up** up to the
   six-slot cap, with **non-maxed levels representative of the configured
   aggression's campaign level**.
3. Every step measures for **at least 15 seconds** (warm-up excluded) and
   records **min, max and average FPS**, alongside the frame-time percentiles,
   long-frame counts and live enemy/bullet counts.
4. The sweep stops at the **first step whose average FPS is below 30**, records
   that step as the failure point, and reports the previous step as the last
   playable load; a documented ceiling/timeout prevents a runaway sweep.
5. The final report is printed to the user as a per-step table plus a headline
   verdict, and the same data is written to a machine-readable JSON report that
   names the scene, step list, loadout **and levels** per step, shoot/dive mix,
   seed, host and commit.
6. The loadout and shoot/dive mix are seeded and recorded; re-running with the
   same seed produces the same loadout sequence and same mixes (unit-tested).
7. The step planner, stop rule and summary are covered by fast unit tests (no
   browser); the scene's parameterised enemy count, loadout and mix seams are
   covered by scene tests; the full suite is green via the test skill and
   typecheck is clean.
8. Gym↔game parity is preserved: the measured scenario runs shared core code,
   any new/changed gym is registered in the capture registry and
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and no simulation loop is forked.
9. Usage is documented (skill docs plus a link from the performance docs /
   README harness section) and one recorded sweep on the reference host is
   published with the provenance the `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` "Recorded:" rule
   requires (commit, date, host, backend, throttle).

## Out of scope

- Optimising anything found by the sweep (a regression or hotspot becomes its
  own child/discovered-from item, per parent AC6).
- Changing the existing budget (60 FPS desktop / >= 30 FPS mobile) or the
  existing `GymPerformance` 100-enemy rows.
- Mobile/CPU-throttled sweeps (the skill may accept `--cpu-throttle` as a
  pass-through, but no throttled sweep is recorded by this item).
- Electron-host sweeps beyond what the existing harness already supports.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
  — parameterise the enemy count, the player loadout and the shoot/dive mix
  (`config.count`, `buildOffsets(count)`, `createEnemyFromConfig`,
  `fireForEnemy`).
- `src/core/perfProbe.ts` — the probe and `PerformanceCounts` seam the sweep
  samples (no change expected).
- `scripts/measure-performance.mjs`, `scripts/perf-launch.mjs`,
  `scripts/perf-report.mjs` — the harness the sweep drives.
- `scripts/perf-sweep.mjs` *(new, likely)* — step planner + sweep driver.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon(id, true)` / `collectPowerUp(id,
  true)` the loadout grant uses.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (six-slot cap the loadout
  respects).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts` — `deploymentLevelForAggression` /
  `hexAggressionLevel` (campaign level the loadout levels derive from).
- `src/core/rules.ts` (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`), `src/powerups/types.ts`,
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — weapon/power-up
  catalogue and level maths.
- `.pi/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` *(new)* — the skill itself (project-local).
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, `README.md` — usage + the recorded sweep.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — only if a gym changes/arrives.

## Notes / constraints

- Measurement policy: agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill; the
  sweep itself is a measurement tool, not a test run, and must not be wired
  into the vitest suite (same rule the existing harness follows).
- Noise floor: compare only within one host load band, and record the host,
  backend and load per step (parent AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 AC6, and the
  `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` noise-floor rule).
- The host can be busy with other agents' suites; the sweep should record each
  step's host load so a noisy sweep is identifiable rather than silently
  published.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The skill may be expected to evolve into a full benchmarking
  or regression-comparison tool. Mitigated by explicit out-of-scope items and
  recording hotspots as separate discovered-from items.
- **Non-determinism from randomness:** Seeded loadouts and mixes reduce but do
  not eliminate concerns about reproducibility across hardware. The seed +
  recorded per-step loadout/levels/mix provide traceability.
- **Sweep duration at high counts:** 400 enemies × 15 s = 600 s minimum; add a
  total-run budget (e.g. 30 min) and enforce a step ceiling.
- **Player-fire decay:** Because the player fires and enemies are not
  invulnerable (producer decision 4), the live enemy count decays within a
  step; N is the peak/target load and the live counts are recorded. If a decayed
  load proves to under-measure sustained load, that becomes a discovered-from
  item, not scope creep.
- **Level derivation:** "Representative of the aggression's campaign level" is
  a documented scaling rule, not a second difficulty system; it reuses
  `hexAggressionLevel`, and the exact scaling constant is tuned at plan time.
- **Gym↔game parity risk:** Adding parameters to `GymFormationScene` must not
  cause a divergence that isn't captured in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`. The parity
  capture tests will flag this.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9` — filed while re-measuring the mobile
  tier on hardware WebGL; the sweep is the natural next step after the fixed
  100-enemy rows.
- Related: **Optimization pass** (AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87) and its performance
  children — **Frame-time performance harness for `PlayScene` (headless
  p50/p95/FPS)** (AH-0MVXV0DER009ER70), **`GymPerformance` stress gym — 100
  late-game enemies with live fire** (AH-0MVXV0DT50028RF8), **Publish
  performance budget, harness usage and results
  (docs/PERFORMANCE.md)** (AH-0MVXV0FUP006W8OR), **Re-measure the mobile tier
  on hardware WebGL and close parent AC5 (4x CPU throttle, quiet host)**
  (AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9).
- Related: **Increase the possible number of enemies in a enemy formation to
  200** (AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5) — the formation cap bounds how large a sweep step
  can be; confirm it before claiming a 200+ step is reachable.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded from the interactive intake interview (producer replies, this session).

- **Q1 — Where does the skill live?** Project-local `.pi/skills/` or a global
  skill? — **Answer (producer):** "project-local". Source: interactive reply,
  2026-11-06.
- **Q2 — What is a "full loadout"?** Which weapons/upgrades, random subset of a
  maxed set or fixed maxed slots, whether power-up levels are maxed —
  **Answer (producer):** "Semi-Random, include weapons from each broad category
  and at least one power-up. Don't max the levels — make them somewhat
  representative of the level they would be if attacking a hex of the defined
  aggression." Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Research: the shipped
  seams are `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)` / `Player.collectPowerUp(id, true)`,
  the six-slot cap is `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`, and `deploymentLevelForAggression`
  → `hexAggressionLevel` maps aggression to campaign level 1–10.
- **Q3 — What is the shoot-and-dive archetype mix?** Which archetypes shoot vs
  dive, and in what proportion — **Answer (producer):** "vary them". Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Interpretation: the proportion varies per step,
  seeded and recorded; the fixable roster includes the stress gym's `diver` and
  `raider`.
- **Q4 — Does the player shoot?** — **Answer (producer):** "Yes". Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Interpretation: auto-fire on; enemies are not
  made invulnerable; live counts recorded.
- **Q5 — How do we keep steps comparable?** — **Answer (producer):** "fix seed +
  duration". Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Interpretation: as-played
  deterministic mode; one seed + fixed per-step duration; kill-free enemies not
  used.
